speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To determine the cause of your visual disturbances, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually, and do you have any floaters or flashes of light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and recent fungal esophagitis, is your vision loss accompanied by any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow? REQUEST TEST: Fluorescein_angiography; REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_photography_right_eye.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy reveals granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4_T-lymphocyte count is 36/mm3. Vital signs: Temperature 37°C (98.6°F), Blood Pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 89/min, Weight 45 kg (99 lbs), Height 170 cm (5 ft 7 in), BMI 15.6 kg/m2. General Examination shows Cervical Lymphadenopathy Present and Skin Examination reveals Multiple violaceous plaques over the trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis.

The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages in an AIDS patient with a CD4 count of 36/mm³ are classic for CMV retinitis. The presence of Kaposi's sarcoma and esophageal fungal infection further supports advanced immunosuppression, but the specific retinal pathology points to CMV as the primary cause of your vision loss.
